sentences.text: The smaller species of this group were about the size of an emperor penguin.
The largest species measured nearly 1.5 meters in height.
The largest species, Palaeeudyptes klekowskii, was estimated to reach 2 meters in length and weigh up to 116 kilograms.
The genus Palaeeudyptes was described by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1859.
The type species of the genus Palaeeudyptes is Palaeeudyptes antarcticus.
The genus Eosphaeniscus, described by Wiman in 1905, is a synonym of Palaeeudyptes.
The genus Palaeeudyptes is the namesake for the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae.
The supposed genus Wimanornis, based on two humeri from Seymour Island, appears to be a more modern synonym of P. gunnari.
The osteological characteristics of Palaeeudyptes were somewhat less advanced than those of Archaeospheniscus and roughly comparable to the gigantic Anthropornis.
The exact evolutionary relationship between the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae and modern penguins is unknown.
The genus Palaeeudyptes existed from the Lutetian to the Burdigalian stages, between 48.07 and 15.98 million years ago.
A humerus identified as Palaeeudyptes was recovered from middle to late Eocene beds near Puerto Natales, southernmost Chile.
